title: Baking sourdough in a Dutch oven
subtitle: Why a covered pot gives home bakers the crust and spring of a professional oven
excerpt: A Dutch oven mimics the steam-injected deck oven of a professional bakery at home. The lid traps steam from the dough itself in the first 20 minutes of baking, keeping the crust pliable while the loaf springs. Removing the lid for the final 20 minutes browns and crisps the crust.
sourceNotes: The Dutch oven method for home sourdough baking is a widely established technique. Temperatures and timing are standard across contemporary sourdough baking practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: Introducing steam into the oven during the first stage of baking to keep the crust soft and extensible while the loaf springs upward. Steam from the dough trapped inside the Dutch oven achieves the same result as steam-injected professional ovens.
The rapid rise that occurs in the first 10 to 15 minutes of baking as gas inside the dough expands with heat. Steam keeps the crust pliable long enough for the full spring to happen.

Place the Dutch oven with its lid inside the oven and heat to 250°C (conventional) for at least 45 minutes. The pot must be scorching hot before the dough goes in, this is what gives the initial blast of heat that drives oven spring. Domestic ovens drift by 20°C or more. An oven thermometer confirms the true temperature before you start. If you find your bakes consistently over or under-doing, that is the first place to look.
Cut a square of baking paper slightly larger than the base of the loaf. Place the cold, scored loaf on it.
Pull the Dutch oven from the oven. Remove the lid. Lower the loaf on its baking paper into the pot using the paper as a sling.
Replace the lid quickly. Return the pot to the oven. Bake at 250°C for 20 minutes.
Remove the lid. Drop the temperature to 230°C. Bake for a further 20 to 25 minutes, until the crust is deep brown and the loaf sounds hollow when you tap the base. An internal probe should read 96°C.
Cool on a wire rack for at least an hour before cutting. The crumb sets as it cools; cutting too soon produces a gummy interior even from a perfectly baked loaf.
The Dutch oven and its lid are extremely hot throughout baking. Use two thick oven gloves. The baking paper sling removes the need to reach into the pot directly.
